provenance.note: All sizes and layouts below are extracted from the pinned revision's headers (atlas/reference/wire/*) and verified by static_assert in the source. This is ground truth, not prose.

alignment.note: messages are padded to 8-byte alignment; all wire objects are 8-aligned

packed_headers.note: message header structs are declared under #pragma pack(push, 1)

message_headers.name: MessageHeaderV1
message_headers.note: used when kFlagExpectsResponse or kFlagIsResponse is set

message_headers.name: MessageHeaderV2
message_headers.note: used when kFlagHasInterfaceId or associated endpoints present

pointer.name: Pointer<T>
pointer.note: offset from the pointer's own address to the target; 0 = null. EncodePointer/DecodePointer in bindings_internal.h

array_header.name: ArrayHeader
array_header.note: element alignment 8 unless packed; inline data follows the header

map_header.note: map encoding = struct { keys: Pointer<Array_Data<K>>, values: Pointer<Array_Data<V>> } (12 bytes padded to 16), validated for equal element counts

string.note: string encoding = struct { ArrayHeader (8 bytes), inline UTF-8 data, NUL terminator, padded to 8 }; no embedded NULs permitted in the payload

union.note: union encoding = struct { uint32 size, uint32 tag } followed by inline data aligned to max(8, field alignment); size covers header+inline data; larger unions are unsupported (>= 2^32-1 rejected)

handles.note: handle values in messages are indices into the message's attached handle list (or associated-endpoint table for interface ids)

validation.note: validation model: relative offsets must be 8-aligned, in-bounds, and non-overlapping (claimed-region tracking); num_bytes checks; version checks; recursion limits; handle-count limits; no trust of attacker lengths; exact error classification via ValidationError enum (see validation_errors.h)
